clarity.justification: The proposal has strong goal-method alignment: it varies only event order in the stated “exact sequence-reversal counterfactual,” compares “directed progression pairs” with “order-invariant comorbidity pairs,” and gives directional, quantified criteria such as “Index ≥ 0.10” and “asymmetry ≥ 3 and prognosis-sign consistency ≥ 0.8.” However, several key quantities remain underspecified: “internal risk/prognosis signal,” “near-zero directed difference,” and the exact outcome head are not operationally defined, and the claim that reversal “flips” the signal is not directly matched to a sign-flip threshold. The logic is nevertheless substantially falsifiable because outcomes such as “asymmetry ≈ 1 and consistency ≈ 0.5” are explicitly identified as negative results, despite minor gaps and overlapping/inconclusive threshold bands.

feasibility.justification: The hardest steps—“build (true order A-before-B) and (reversed order B-before-A) by swapping only the two events' positions/timestamps” and applying “matched-norm perturbations along the axis”—are implementable with standard sequence editing, forward hooks, probes, and activation interventions, not magic steps; the intervention still needs an explicit definition of normalization and layer/readout handling. MIMIC-III/IV are established datasets and probes, random-direction controls, co-occurrence controls, and matched comorbidity reversals are supported by standard PyTorch/interpretability tooling, but no specific released EHR foundation model or universally available “outcome head” is named, so the plan may need to train or attach the risk head and document model-specific interfaces. Resources are meaningfully quantified through “~40k patients,” “~300k,” “~50 DIRECTED progression pairs,” “≥1,000 trajectories per pair class,” and “seeds 0–4”; the refuting branch is runnable because the design includes comorbidity reversals, bag-of-codes baselines, random steering directions, and explicit negative criteria, although the unspecified risk readout leaves some implementation work.
